references.text: The priests shall not make themselves bald on their heads, nor shave the edges of their beards, nor cut gashes in their flesh. This is a parallel law that applies specifically to the priests, with similar prohibitions against altering hair and beard.

You are children of the Lord your God. You shall not cut yourselves or make yourself bald on your forehead for the dead. This verse expands the prohibition and links it to Israel's status as God's holy people.
Cut off your hair and cast it away; raise a lamentation upon the bare hills. Jeremiah uses the cutting of hair as a sign of mourning and judgment, showing the cultural significance of hair.
They shall not shave their heads or let their hair grow wild, but cut it neatly. These are rules for the priests in the future temple, reflecting the same principles regarding appropriate grooming.
Every head is shaved, every beard is shorn as a sign of mourning. Isaiah describes pagan mourning customs that stand in contrast to God's prohibition for Israel.
